what_i_see: Very faint, roughly round diffuse patch ~10" across centred on the field, smooth with no nucleus, a few compact sources superposed. It appears blue in the colour panel while neighbours show NISP colour, so it is detected mainly in VIS.
most_likely: A low-surface-brightness dwarf galaxy, or a faint VIS-only scattered-light feature.
against_it: VIS-only detection fits an optical ghost; no catalogue entry; not visible in a Legacy DR10 cutout (inconclusive, DES is shallower).
decisive_test: Check individual VIS exposures/dithers and a NISP stack: a real galaxy persists at fixed sky position and appears faintly in NISP; a ghost moves or vanishes.
catalogue_notes: No SIMBAD, Gaia, or NED object at centre; nearest NED WISEA J025933.40-540729.3 14.5" S. No DR8 photo-z rows within 12" (likely coverage gap). Brightest nearby Gaia star G=10.6 at 414". No match in Jacobs+2019, Huang+2020/2021 (cone 10"; Rojas+2022 query unvalidated).
